To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chloramphenicol is concentrated in human polymorphonucelar leukocytes (PMNs) by a non-energy dependent process, and chloramphenicole is bactericidal to intracellular H. Influenzae Type B

chloramphenicol but not penicillin is concentrated within polymorphonuclear cells and that chloramphenicolor but not penicillins is active against Haemophilis influenzae type b within polymorphonucelar cells.
chloramphenicol is concentrated in polymorphonuclear neutrophils (PMNLs), and that it is more effective than penicillin against intracellular Haemo-philus influenzae type B.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the intracellular fate of Haemophilus species.
the development of new approaches to the prevention and treatment of infectious diseases.
the development of an experimental model for the study of the intracellular activity of antibacterial agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipid-soluble chloramphenicol is concentrated and is bioactive within PMN.
the PMNLs are capable of concentrating and maintaining intracellularly the lipid-soluble chloramphenicol, but not the water-soluble penicillin.
the PMNL is an important host cell in the defense of the host against H. influenzae infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PMNLs that have phagocytosed opsonized HIB are capable of killing intracellular HIB, and that this killing is enhanced by the intracellular accumulation of chloramphenocol.
chloramphenicol is more active than penicillin or cephalosporins against H. influenzae in human phagocytic cells.
the uptake and activity of antibiotics against intracellular bacteria is an important factor in determining the clinical efficacy of an antibiotic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antibiotics that are not concentrated in phagocytes are less effective at killing intracellular bacteria.
chloramphenicol is a better choice of antibiotic for the treatment of bacterial meningitis than penicillin.
the intracellular activity of an antibiotic is dependent on its ability to penetrate into the phagocytic vacuole and to be concentrated within the phagocyte.
